correctness.rationale: In the stated axiom-only syntax with distinct conjunction and implication constructors, necessity follows immediately by reading the boxed-operand bits from the world’s generated set. For sufficiency let H be the set of true bits in the subformula-closed support S containing top, and P the closure of H under conjunction formation alone if C is present (P=H otherwise). P∩S=H by induction on conjunction formation: the operands of a conjunction in S are in S, and the finite C implications suffice. If M is present, any conjunction in P either came from H, where its parts are in H by the finite M constraints, or was constructed from parts in P. Any implication in P was already in H; if its antecedent is in P, it is in S and hence in H, so K supplies its consequent in H. N is already satisfied in H when selected. Thus P is globally closed under all selected rules and realizes exactly the guessed bits in S. Ordinary Boolean evaluation at a one-world model gives the witness; there are linearly many guessed bits and polynomial-time checks. Modal-free SAT and TAUT give the matching lower bounds, since all propositional assignments extend to suitable one-world models. This confirms the unrestricted proof, with ordinary faithful abbreviations read via the corresponding syntax, not arbitrary rewrites inside boxes. The frozen checker uses separate syntax constructors and 1,568 bounded comparisons; it was inspected, not executed, and the finite checks are not a proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There are O(|φ|) candidate bits. For each query, the polynomial-size subformula support is listed directly from the candidate; every nonfinal stage adds at least one member. Each stage checks only polynomially many candidate formulas or pairs, hence membership is polynomial, even with a naive implementation. Guess one candidate and evaluate φ to check satisfiability (or its falsity to check nonvalidity). The same modal-free lower bounds are immediate. Thus the exact classification and linear-size guessing bound follow from reading the complexity of the published algorithm, without a new finite-support lemma.

originality.rationale: Nishimura’s Corollary 3.14 already gives linear-size one-point candidate descriptions and explicitly states the same finite subformula restriction for closure membership. The stages of Definition 3.7 are just monotone forward chaining of the four Horn rules over those formulas. Counting additions per stage rather than accepting the paper’s loose primitive-recursive bound makes the NP/coNP classification immediate. The complexity labels are sharper than the published labels, but the candidate space and the load-bearing finite-support algorithm are already in the proof for exactly the same sixteen logics.
residual_risks: The bounded inspection does not determine who first stated the tighter complexity labels in print. The failure rests on a direct implication of an inspected proof, not on the possibility of other earlier complexity results.

value.rationale: Optimal formula complexity is a legitimate question. Here the gap between primitive recursiveness and coNP closes by counting stages in the same previously published subformula computation and guessing one of its already published linear-size candidates. The Horn presentation is a convenient reformulation, not an independently useful new decision algorithm or structural lemma beyond that computation. No substantive remainder warrants a repair.
